successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: the Nabataean Kingdom, which Trajan's army annexed as the province of Arabia Petraea with Bosra as capital

ledger.x: 169 BC: Aretas I, 'the tyrant of the Arabs', is the first named Nabataean king.
144: the Jordan's east bank passes to Judea.
126: the Negev and the Sinai coast are added to the shape.

c. 96: Alexander Jannaeus takes northern Moab and Gilead from the Nabataeans. 'Alexander Jannaeus captured northern Moab and Gilead, threatening Nabataean trade' (undated); the page puts his occupation of Gaza in 96, used only as the earliest plausible year. The Nabataeans page: he 'invaded and occupied the Nabataean…

c. 93: Obodas I regains Moab and Gilead. 'Obodas I regained these areas around 93 BC' and defeated Jannaeus at the Battle of Gadara around 93; the Nabataeans page puts the ambush near Gaulane in 90 BC, and has him 'destroying the Judaean army'. [Fix 2026-10-19: the Hasmonean dynasty page (opened): 'In 93 BC at the…
63: Damascus passes to the Roman Republic.
62 BC: Aretas III becomes a Roman vassal.
27 BC: the client relation passes from the Republic to the Empire.
27 BC: Nabataea is a client of the Roman Empire until the annexation of 106.

c. 24 BC: the Nabataeans annex Lihyan. The Lihyan page (opened 2026-10-19): 'Werner Caskel suggests that the Nabataean annexation of Lihyan was around 24 BC'; 'Some authors assert that the Lihyanites fell into the hands of the Nabataeans around 65 BC upon their seizure of Hegra then marching to Tayma, and finally to…
106: Trajan annexes the kingdom as Arabia Petraea; the client relation ends with it. roman-empire records its vassal_end in 106 and its gain in 106.
106: Trajan annexes the Nabataean Kingdom as the province of Arabia Petraea, with Bosra as capital.

wars.name: Nabataean wars with Alexander Jannaeus
wars.outcome: Jannaeus took Gaza (96) and northern Moab and Gilead; Obodas I regained them around 93 and ambushed him near Gaulane (90 on the Nabataeans page).

wars.name: Tigranes II's siege of Damascus
wars.outcome: Tigranes took Damascus from Aretas III in 72; his forces were pulled out in 69 and Aretas retook the city.

wars.name: Hyrcanus II and Aristobulus II: Aretas III's siege of Jerusalem and Scaurus's march on Petra
wars.outcome: Aretas besieged Jerusalem with 50,000 men for several months for Hyrcanus II; Scaurus, bribed by Aristobulus, ordered him away, and in 62 marched on Petra; Aretas paid several hundred talents and recognised Roman supremacy.

wars.name: Herod's war on Nabataea
wars.outcome: 'In 32 BC, during King Malichus I's reign, Herod the Great, with the support of Cleopatra, started a war against Nabataea'; his forces 'overran Nabataea' a year later.

wars.name: Aretas IV's war with Herod Antipas
wars.outcome: 'Aretas invaded Herod Antipas' domain and defeated his army'; Vitellius moved south with his legions, stopping in Jerusalem 'for the passover of AD 37'.

wars.name: Roman annexation of Nabataea
wars.outcome: Trajan refused to recognise any claimant after Rabbel II's death and annexed the kingdom as Arabia Petraea (106), capital Bosra; Petra became a metropolis.

certainty.note: Desert and caravan-route frontiers, named by towns (Petra, Hegra, Bosra, Damascus, the Negev towns), never by a surveyed line; the Roman limes arabicus after 106 is outside the kingdom.
